proof: `CALENDAR 2013 WAGES`, PDF pages 93-97 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed pages 89-93): every person the Town paid in calendar 2013, with their department and their gross wages. Five pages, 544 names. NO PAGE HAS A TEXT LAYER; each was read off its own 400 dpi bitmap. PAGE 93 IS THE FIRST PAGE OF THIS RUN AND IT WAS NOT IN THE PAGE TRACKER. The tracker admits a page on fifteen recognised money figures and recognition found seventeen words on this one, so it was ABSENT rather than unfinished -- 130 names, A to D, invisible to every count of what remains. It was found by sweeping every page of the report for money figures against the tracker's own list, which is the extent check `READING-A-REPORT-PAGE.md` prescribes. THE COLUMN NAMES HERE ARE OURS, AND THAT IS SAID RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The only thing printed over this table is `CALENDAR 2013 WAGES`, above the money column. The three columns to its left carry NO printed heading at all, so `fund_number` (surname), `fund_name` (forename and department) and `gross_wages` are labels WE have given to what the cells visibly contain. Rule 13b.4 says never infer a column name from the words at the top of a page; here there are no words to infer from, and the honest statement is that the document does not name them. EACH PAGE PRINTS TWO LABEL/NAME/DEPARTMENT/AMOUNT COLUMN-PAIRS and they are ONE list, not two: page 93 runs ADAMOWICZ to BRAND down the left and BRANHAM to DAVIS down the right, so the alphabet continues from one pair into the next. That is unlike FY2022, whose two columns are separately alphabetised A-Z and must not be merged; it was checked here rather than assumed. THE PAGES PRINT NO TOTAL OF ANY KIND -- not per page, not per department, not for the run -- so there is no arithmetic to close and THE CHECK IS COVERAGE, declared and weaker. Two assertions, and they catch different failures: `rows_per_page` = 130, which every page but the last carries exactly (the last carries 24), catches a single name skipped; and `ordered_by` surname, which runs forward through all 544 rows without going backwards once, catches a page or a block dropped. NEITHER CAN SEE A MISREAD DIGIT. A wrong figure in this file survives both checks untouched, and nothing in the archive states these wages a second time. READ AS PRINTED, INCLUDING WHERE THE PAGE TRUNCATES. Several surnames are cut off by their cell and are recorded truncated rather than guessed: `CARPENTER BO`, `COURTEMANC`, `MCCARTHY-GU`, `MITCHELL-TAR`, `PAPADOPOULO`, `VAILLANCOUR`. `MC CARTHY` is printed with a space and `MCBRIDE` without, on adjacent rows, and both stand. WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT (CLAUDE.md rules 7 and 11). It is GROSS WAGES PAID in a CALENDAR year to named people, by the department that paid them. It is NOT a fiscal-year figure, so it cannot be differenced against any budget line in this report, which are all FY2013. It is NOT a headcount of positions: a person paid by two departments appears twice, and a name with $48.00 beside it and a name with $126,540.42 are one row each. It carries NO FTE and NO funding source, so it cannot say whether a post was full time or which fund paid for it -- the same limit the staff rosters have, already registered in `money-gaps.csv`. And it is wages only: it excludes every benefit, so it is not what any of these people cost the town.
